To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Canadian approach to developing quality assurance standards has been successful in developing standards for commissioning and for quality control of equipment used in Radiation Oncology, and that the Abt III Study of Medical Physicist Work Values provides a means of justifying staffing levels and work values for radiation oncology medical physics services.
the Canadian approach to standards is a good model for developing standards for radiation oncology, and the Abt III report is an excellent tool for justifying medical physics staffing.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(a) the development of Quality Control Standards in Radiation Oncology; and (b) the use of these standards to support the staffing and cost justification of radiation oncology medical physics services.
developing and applying new methods to improve the quality of medical physics services and to justify the medical physicists' work.
the development of Quality Control Standards for radiation oncology physics services, and with how these standards are used to justify the staffing and work of medical physicists.

the medical physicist must understand how to develop standards and defend staffing for radiation oncology.

there is a need for a comprehensive and detailed approach to the development of Quality Control Standards in Radiation Oncology, and that there is a clear need to justify the staffing required for the development and implementation of these standards.
the medical physicist has a crucial role in ensuring the safety and quality in the delivery of radiotherapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Canadian approach to the development of standards is a novel approach that is more inclusive than traditional expert panels.

medical physics has developed standards for the commissioning and quality assurance of radiation therapy equipment and procedures that are evidence based, and that these standards are supported by staffing and billing information.
the Canadian standards process, the AAPM TG process and the evidence based approach are complimentary and should all be used to improve quality and safety.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the medical physicist must be able to justify the work that he/she does to the institution.
the Canadian standards development model is a very effective way to develop standards that are broadly accepted and used by the Canadian medical physics community.

the medical physics profession has the responsibility and obligation to ensure that all of the standards for commissioning and QC of radiation therapy equipment, and the staffing to accomplish those standards, are evidence based and are justified to all stakeholders, including patients and payers.
